findings.summary: After one Tab press the Delivery window select looks exactly as at rest: `button:focus, select:focus { outline: none; }` removes the focus indicator from every control, so keyboard users cannot see where they are.
findings.fix: Replace the rule with `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ay-color-focus); outline-offset: 2px; }` on the select and both buttons.

findings.summary: The help text that explains what happens when nobody is home is #838383 on #ffffff, about 3.8:1, below the 4.5:1 floor for body text; low-vision users may miss the five-day depot rule.
findings.fix: Use the label text token (--ay-color-text-label, #4f5a6b, about 7:1).

findings.summary: The help button is 32 x 32 px, under the 44 x 44 px floor, and sits next to Save, so a missed tap can hit the wrong control on a phone.
findings.fix: Make it the icon button size of the cozy density (--ay-size-control-height, 44 px) on both axes.

findings.summary: The help button shows only "?"; its accessible name is clear, but sighted first-time users cannot tell what help it offers.
findings.fix: Optional: add the visible text "What do the windows mean?" or a tooltip.

personas.note: Tab reaches the select and both buttons, but nothing shows which one has focus, so choosing a window and saving is guesswork.
The tree names the heading, the labelled combobox, and both buttons; the help button's name is announced.
The 3.8:1 help text is hard to read when zoomed, and the missing focus ring makes the current control hard to find.
The task is clear: pick a window and save; the "?" button's purpose is not obvious.
